description: Increased bleeding risk when an anticoagulant is combined with an antiplatelet agent.
NSAIDs increase bleeding risk when combined with warfarin.
Regular or high-dose paracetamol can raise INR and increase the anticoagulant effect of warfarin.
source_note: Documented with regular use; occasional single doses matter less.

description: Penicillins can reduce methotrexate clearance, raising the risk of methotrexate toxicity.
Ciprofloxacin can raise theophylline levels, increasing the risk of toxicity.
Clarithromycin greatly raises simvastatin levels, increasing the risk of serious muscle damage (rhabdomyolysis).
source_note: Strong CYP3A4 inhibition; contraindicated on labels.

description: Potassium loss from furosemide can increase digoxin toxicity.
NSAIDs can blunt the blood-pressure effect of ACE inhibitors and strain the kidneys.
Combined use raises the risk of serotonin syndrome and seizures.
Ibuprofen can interfere with the heart-protective effect of low-dose aspirin if taken close together.
Furosemide can raise metformin levels, and diuretics can affect blood-sugar control.
Omeprazole can reduce how well clopidogrel works.
source_note: CYP2C19 interaction; noted on clopidogrel labelling.

description: Amlodipine raises simvastatin levels, increasing muscle-damage risk at higher simvastatin doses.
NSAIDs can weaken the blood-pressure effect of losartan and affect kidney function.
source_note: Same class effect as ACE inhibitor plus NSAID.

description: Calcium can block absorption of levothyroxine unless doses are spaced apart.
Calcium can block absorption of ciprofloxacin unless doses are spaced apart.
Corticosteroids plus NSAIDs raise the risk of stomach ulcers and bleeding.
NSAIDs can reduce methotrexate clearance and raise toxicity risk, especially at high methotrexate doses.
Together they can cause dangerously high potassium (hyperkalaemia).
Combined use raises the risk of serotonin syndrome and seizures.
source_note: Same class as sertraline and tramadol.

description: Combined antiplatelet use raises bleeding risk; sometimes prescribed together on purpose under supervision.
Together they can cause dangerously high potassium.
Raises the risk of dangerous heart rhythm changes (QT prolongation).
source_note: Contraindicated on labelling in several markets.

description: Omeprazole can raise citalopram levels; citalopram dose limits apply.
Metronidazole can greatly increase warfarin's blood-thinning effect.
Amiodarone raises digoxin levels sharply, risking toxicity.
Amiodarone increases warfarin's effect and bleeding risk.
Together they can cause dangerously high potassium.
